evidence.quote: US 708 is an extremely He-rich sdO star in the Galaxy halo, with a heliocentric radial velocity of+ 7 0 8 \pm 1 5 \mathrm { k m / s }(Hirsch et al. [61]).

notes: US 708 (T:p1-b4, T:p4-b2, T:p5-b3): The paper treats it as a previously identified halo HVS; its explicit definition of an HVS as a star able to escape the Galaxy supplies the unbound criterion, and the cited high radial velocity places US 708 in that class. The discussion uses US 708 as a comparison for a surviving-companion origin, so this is follow_up rather than a newly selected candidates_found object. No Gaia identifier is supplied.

US 708: US 708 is discussed only as a comparison object; the paper reports no position, distance, parallax, proper motion, Galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for it.
